notes: Correct and complete, but it adds somewhat superfluous parser wrapper methods alongside the Token helpers, and most tests only assert no error and the segment count.
Correct and complete, but it adds a redundant parser-level wrapper layer placed oddly at the end of the file, and the tests mostly check only error and segment count.
It misses the nested branch of NextBlock, so a quoted '{' or '}' reached via d.Next() in a block can still change nesting; its ParseAll test checks only keys.

Misses NextBlock's nested-level branch, so a quoted '}' or '{' at end of line still changes nesting when tokens are walked without consuming args (e.g. NextSegment in handle { route { respond "}" } }); the tests don't catch this.
Dispenser helpers plus inline checks cover all sites correctly, but only three minimal table tests were added.
Covers all sites, mixing Dispenser helpers with inline checks; only three minimal table tests were added.
Complete and correct, including the doImport check, but it repeats `Val()==... && !Quoted()` inline everywhere instead of a helper; tests check segment counts only.
Covers every site, but repeats the inline Val()/Quoted() check everywhere instead of using a helper; reasonable table tests.
Helpers on both Token and Dispenser cover every site; tests are strong (dispenser, parse, unbalanced-brace errors, adapt test), though the redundant quoted check is kept.
Complete fix that leaves a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive(); tests are thorough (dispenser, segments, snippets, unbalanced-brace errors, adapt test).

Unquoted-brace helpers on Token are applied at every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser, matching the reference; it keeps a now-redundant wasQuoted check in directive() and skips the minor HasSuffix and '{}' tweaks, but its dispenser and parse tests are solid.
Clean fix using Token methods that mirrors the reference; good dispenser and parser tests including snippet import.
Inline Quoted() checks everywhere work but are repetitive, miss the doImport anonymous-block check and keep the redundant wasQuoted check; tests only verify segment counts.
Repetitive inline checks, misses the doImport anonymous-block guard, and leaves a redundant wasQuoted check; the main bug is fixed.
Dispenser-level helpers fix the core issue, but it leaves the doImport anonymous-block check comparing raw text and mixes inline checks with helpers; parse subtests are decent.
Mostly complete fix, but it leaves the doImport 'anonymous blocks' check unguarded and mixes helpers with inline checks; the subtests verifying segment tokens are good.
Complete, clean Token-helper fix covering every site; it adds thorough parse tests (including an expected-error case and snippets/import blocks) plus a fitting caddyfile_adapt integration test.
Complete fix with Token helpers; very thorough tests (segments, keys, an unbalanced error case, snippet block import, adapt test).
Complete, correct Token-helper fix with good unit tests; the added live-server integration test is heavier than needed and the addresses check is inlined.
Complete, clean fix; the dispenser test exercises NextBlock's nested branch without consuming args, and it adds a somewhat heavy live-server integration test.
Clean, complete helper-based fix with the redundant check removed; reasonable table tests covering arguments, blocks and the non-braced site form.

Covers every structural brace check in the dispenser and parser through Token and Dispenser helpers; like most candidates it skips the quoted address HasSuffix check and the quoted '{}' case, and the table tests include a nested case.
Essentially the reference approach, with clean Token helpers and the redundant quoted check removed; tests are concise table entries that check segment counts only.
Essentially C4's implementation with the redundant check removed; adequate table tests including a nested block case.
Token helpers plus bounds-checked Dispenser atOpenBrace/atCloseBrace are applied everywhere; good dispenser test of nesting and post-block position plus parse table cases.
Complete fix with clear atOpenBrace/atCloseBrace helpers; good dispenser and table tests.
Same clean design as the reference; its NextBlock test with a lone quoted '}' line exercises the dispenser nesting path well.
Complete fix; its NextBlock dispenser test iterates without consuming args, which specifically guards the nested-branch change.
Clean, layered Token and Dispenser helpers applied consistently with the redundant check removed; good dispenser and parse tests including backtick and nested cases.
Complete, well-structured fix with safe Token and Dispenser helpers; solid dispenser and parse tests including snippet import.
Bounds-checked Dispenser helpers cover all sites, though doImport and addresses use inline checks and the redundant wasQuoted check remains; good dispenser and parse tests.
Correct and complete with Dispenser helpers plus some inline wasQuoted checks; good tests, though the helper usage is slightly inconsistent.
Owner-claim fix; its unit test enshrines dropping the child's distinct instance q under a misleading 'identical blocks' comment, on an odd fixture without for_each.
Fixes the root-module case, but its new unit test explicitly asserts that child block b["q"] is dropped because the parent imports b["p"], which locks in the residual silent-drop bug.
Linear-scan override with a reasonable context test using provider fns, but the same incomplete resource-level parent/child override.
An O(n²) linear scan keeps same-module blocks, but the cross-module whole-resource override still drops child blocks for distinct instances.
Groups statements per ConfigResource and keeps same-module blocks, but parent blocks still override every child block for that resource regardless of instance.
Map-of-slices fix for the same-module case; parent-over-child override remains per config resource rather than per instance.
Map-of-slices variant that fixes root for_each imports but keeps resource-level cross-module override that discards child blocks for other instances.
Grouping statements as Map[ConfigResource][]ImportStatement fixes the same-module case, but keeps whole-resource cross-module override and so loses child instance imports.
Clean owner-claim fix with a thorough unit test, but that test explicitly locks in silently dropping child instance 'c' when the parent imports other instances.
Code fixes the same-module case, but the thorough unit test codifies dropping child overridden["c"] even though the parent never targets that instance.

Moves dedup to per-instance by re-parsing static `to` keys at config time, which fixes the reported bug and the static cross-module case, but it ignores module-instance keys and conservatively drops child blocks whenever a key is dynamic (hidden 2/3).

Moves the override to static instance-key comparison, so distinct parent/child instances are both kept, but any for_each or dynamic block (or a module-instance-keyed target) conservatively drops the whole child block; it also adds HCL parsing to the refactoring package.
Owner-module claim map fixes same-module for_each imports, but a parent still silently overrides child blocks that target different instances.
Tidy claimed-map approach that fixes the issue's repro, but dedup still happens before expansion at ConfigResource granularity across modules.
Map of slices grouped by ConfigResource fixes the root-module case but keeps resource-level cross-module override that discards distinct child instances.
A clean map-of-slices variant that fixes the repro but leaves cross-module instance imports subject to silent drop.
Keeps all same-module blocks, but a parent block still claims the whole ConfigResource, so child blocks for other instances are silently dropped, the same class of bug as the issue.
Fixes the reported scenario; cross-module dedup remains at ConfigResource level, so child instance imports can still vanish silently.
Owner-claim approach using string-keyed maps instead of addrs.Map; adds a unit test, but cross-module override remains at resource rather than instance granularity.
Uses a string-keyed owner map and adds reasonable unit and context tests, but keeps the whole-resource cross-module override instead of deferring dedup to instance expansion.
Linear-scan override check keeps same-module blocks but applies parent override at ConfigResource level, losing distinct child instance imports.
Same linear-scan approach as C4: it fixes the reported repro but leaves the module-level silent-drop variant of the bug.

Returns all statements children-first so the parent's later Put wins per instance during expansion, achieving instance-level override with a minimal change. It relies implicitly on overwrite semantics in node_resource_plan.go and has no test for the module-ordering contract.

Removes pre-expansion dedup and orders children before parents so the parent wins via map overwrite during expansion; this is correct and simpler than the reference, though it relies implicitly on Put-overwrite ordering, and the test covers only the root case.
Owner-claim map fixes the reported scenario; cross-module dedup still happens before instance expansion, so distinct child instances can be silently lost.
Owner-map fix for same-module blocks, but it still discards child instance imports whenever a parent targets the same resource.
Same owner-claim approach with a test covering root plus child for_each imports, but it never exercises or fixes the parent-vs-child different-instance override.

Keeps all same-module blocks, which fixes the reported repro, but still overrides at the ConfigResource level across modules, so a child block for a different instance than the parent's is still silently dropped.
Pointer-slice owner-claim variant that fixes the reported case but still drops child blocks for other instances when a parent targets the same resource.

Clean owner-map approach (plus a defensive slice-aliasing fix) that fixes the root-module case, but child-module blocks for other instances are still discarded whenever a parent targets the same resource.
Owner-claim approach with a unit test covering only single-instance override; the different-instance parent/child case remains broken.
Fixes the root-module case with sensible tests, but still overrides child blocks per config resource rather than per instance.

Applies slugs to a regular page only when its container dir equals the section base, so pages in non-section subdirectories keep the old path; it also does ad-hoc tree lookups with an odd length check.

It only rewrites the dir when it equals the section base, so pages in non-section subdirs keep the unslugged path; it also reaches into treePages directly, which is fragile, and it fails a hidden test.
Correct in normal cases, but it has a pointless always-nil error return and the same lowercase-vs-unnormalized matching fragility.
It works via a lowercased path-prefix map, but has an always-nil error return, two separate override fields, and the same disablePathToLower normalization mismatch risk as C5.

Works in normal configurations, but it matches on lowercased Path() against possibly unnormalized dirs, which can miss slugs under disablePathToLower when names contain spaces or other normalized characters.
The lowercased prefix matching against Path() works in normal setups but can mismatch under disablePathToLower; the separate SectionBase and ContainerDir fields are reasonable.
Prefix-map replacement is correct, but it builds the result into ExpandedPermalink and skips the normal permalink handling, which overloads a field meant for configured permalinks.
It produces correct paths but does so by hijacking ExpandedPermalink, conflating slug paths with permalink config, which is fragile with uglyURLs and sub-resources.
Overloads the permalink path (opath/ExpandedPermalink) to carry the slugged path, and a slugged section replaces its whole relative path, dropping intermediate non-section dirs.
The chain-based TrimPrefix construction is correct, but routing the result through the permalink expansion path (QueryUnescape, 'expanded permalink' logging) is a hack.
Replaces a page's whole container dir with the current section's slugged path, so directories between the section and the page are lost (fails a hidden test).

It replaces a regular page's entire container dir with the section path, which drops non-section subdirs; it also replaces multi-segment relative section paths wholesale with the slug, and it fails a hidden test.
Clean depth-based slug replacement gated on no permalink, no URL and not home; the tests don't cover pages in non-section subdirectories.
Depth-indexed segment replacement over ancestors (plus self for branches) is correct and is skipped when a permalink or URL applies; the tests mostly assert file existence only.
Clean slug map on the descriptor with prefix replacement in both branches, consistent with path normalization; the tests are adequate but miss deeper directory cases.
A clean slug map applied by path prefix in CreateTargetPaths, with correct unnormalized handling and good coverage of sections, taxonomy and term.
Same robust path→slug map approach as C1 but cleaner, with a small helper that collects the slugged sections.
It passes a map from section base to slug into the descriptor and applies it by full-prefix matching, which handles unnormalized paths and non-section dirs cleanly.
Same lowercase-matching fragility as C12, but otherwise a simple, focused implementation with reasonable tests.
It matches via strings.ToLower(prefix) against the normalized Path(), which can miss under disablePathToLower when names need more than lowercasing (e.g. spaces); otherwise correct.
Indexes segments by SectionsEntries depth, which correctly handles deep and intermediate dirs; the tests are thorough, covering ugly URLs and taxonomy/term with auto-created terms.

It indexes by SectionsEntries length, which handles non-direct parent sections, and it has the strongest tests (deep sections, uglyURLs, taxonomy/term); it also makes a small unnecessary change dropping the empty-dir check.

Passes the section's own path and each ancestor's path with its slug into the descriptor, then swaps matching prefix elements in both the branch and the page dirs; robust to normalization and intermediate dirs, though the unchecked `*pageState` type assertion is slightly fragile.
The prefix-map approach in the page package is correct, but it uses an unchecked sp.(*pageState) type assertion where sp.Slug() would suffice.
Concise walk up the parent chain with depth-based replacement and cmp.Or fallback; tests cover deep non-section dirs, leaf bundles and taxonomy/term slugs.
A concise walk up CurrentSection/Parent that replaces segments by path depth, with cmp.Or fallbacks; its tests cover deep non-section dirs, nested slugged sections and taxonomy/term.
Depth-based segment replacement is simple and handles deep non-section dirs and taxonomies; the docs edits are relevant but go beyond what was required.

It indexes each slugged ancestor by its path depth over the full container dir, so nested sections, non-section subdirs and taxonomies/terms all work; the docs edits are related but go beyond what the task needed.

Rebuilds the section dir from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, so non-section intermediate dirs between nested sections (e.g. /a/b/c whose parent is /a) are dropped whenever any slug is set; the common cases work.

It rebuilds the path from each section's BaseNameNoIdentifier, which drops intermediate non-section dirs (e.g. /help/sub/deep becomes /ayuda/deep); otherwise it is sound and appends the remaining container dir for regular pages.
Skips slug application entirely for pages whose container dir is not the section itself, so descendants in subdirectories are not localized (fails a hidden test).
It returns no slug path for regular pages not directly in their section, so descendants in non-section subdirs keep the original dir; it fails a hidden test.
Internal implementation that always sets Exec explicitly, which is harmless. Tests cover unit behaviour and archive but include no run integration test.

Keeps the logic in internal/cmd and applies it after consolidation, but always sets Exec valid (so 'exec: default' shows in descriptions) and does not drop shortcuts from lower config layers or reject execution-segment flags.
Places a CLI-message helper (OnceConflictError) in lib/executor, which is a poor layering choice. Its tests are thinner: one conflict flag, no env check, and no archive.
Works, but puts a CLI error constructor (OnceConflictError) in the public lib/executor package and always marks Exec as valid.

Applies the transform after consolidation and registers the flag on run, archive and cloud run. ApplyOnce lands in the public lib/executor package. Like the other candidates, it does not drop env/config-layer shortcuts, so they can still wipe script scenarios before the transform runs.
Clean applyOnceFlag wrapper and an exported ApplyOnce in lib; the flag is added to cloud run only, and the tests are reasonable but appended to the huge cmd_run_test.go.
Works correctly and guards against a nil cmd. Integration tests cover only one conflict flag and there is no archive test. It shares the lower-layer shortcut gap.

Solid post-consolidation transform with good integration and unit tests, but adds a CLI-specific exported ApplyOnce to the public lib/executor package and ignores lower-layer shortcuts that can wipe the script's scenarios.

Validates conflicts early in loadAndConfigureLocalTest and lists every conflicting flag. Tests are excellent, covering setup/teardown order, env/tags, archive and non-mutation. It misses lower-layer shortcut handling and puts CLI-specific logic in lib/executor.
Well-rounded: early conflict validation that lists all conflicting flags, a help example, and comprehensive tests (full struct equality, input not mutated); the downside is the exported lib API.

Keeps the logic internal to cmd, detects conflicts via the CLI options, and lists scenario names in the error. Has strong unit, integration and archive tests. It still misses env/config shortcuts dropping scenarios during the merge.

Internal implementation that checks conflicts from the CLI options layer and lists sorted names in the multi-scenario error, with strong unit, integration and archive tests; does not drop shortcuts from lower layers.
Implementation is correct for the main path but silently ignores the GetBool error, and ApplyOnce lives in the public lib. It has a reasonable integration and unit test set, with no archive coverage.
Correct and compact, but silently ignores the GetBool error, exports ApplyOnce from lib/executor, and shares the lower-layer and execution-segment gaps.
Compact internal implementation with proper exit codes. It ships only unit tests in config_test.go, with no integration or archive coverage of actual runs.
Minimal and correct internal implementation with precise exec handling, but only unit tests and no end-to-end run or archive coverage.
Correct after-consolidation transform with Counter-based integration tests and an archive check. The conflict assertions do not verify the flag name, and ApplyOnce sits in the public lib.
Good tests (counter tags, setup/teardown, archive metadata), but the core logic is an exported ApplyOnce in lib/executor and the existing err declaration is reshuffled slightly.

Uses two layers: a cmd wrapper calling lib/executor.ApplyOnce. Tests are strong, including archive and an empty-scenarios case. The test helper reimplements strings.Count, and the lower-layer shortcut gap remains.

Thorough tests including a derive round-trip and archive metadata; exports ApplyOnce in lib, wires the flag to cloud run only (not the deprecated cloud command), and uses a hand-rolled countOccurrences helper.
Has a well-organized internal once.go with a sentinel error. Tests are thorough: flag validation including short flags, exec/env/tags/scenario name, setup/teardown, and archive via ReadArchive.

Clean internal/cmd implementation with a dedicated flag set on run/archive/cloud, correct exec handling, and very thorough tests (setup/teardown, env/tags, archive, all conflicts); misses the lower-layer shortcut drop.

A clean internal applyOnceFlag with sorted scenario names in the error. Tests are comprehensive, including top-level vus plus scenarios and an archive metadata check. The final gjson assertion is clunky.
Self-contained internal applyOnceFlag with sorted scenario names in errors, a help example, and comprehensive unit, integration and archive tests; misses dropping shortcuts from lower layers.

Implementation is clean and placed after consolidation. Tests check JSON iteration counts with tags, but the env check via throw is weak because exceptions still count as iterations, and there is no archive test.
Correct exported ApplyOnce with reasonable tests, though the test file name doesn't match the source file and a duplicate sum helper is added.
Solid implementation, and its integration test uses startTime '1h' to prove scenario fields are discarded. It has no archive test and keeps ApplyOnce in the public lib.
Correct, with good integration tests (startTime discarded, tags and json results), but adds an exported ApplyOnce to lib/executor and shares the lower-layer gap.
Logic is placed in config.go and keeps an explicit default exec. Has good integration tests including setup/teardown and archive, though the archive test only checks the default scenario.
Functional internal implementation with good tests, but rebuilds BaseConfig with a hardcoded 'shared-iterations' string and always sets Exec valid.
Works, but adds a redundant OnceScenarioError type alongside ExecutionConflictError and isOnceSet swallows errors. Tests are spread across run, archive and executor files.
Works, but adds an unnecessary exported custom error type and a DeriveOnceScenarios API to lib/executor, and isOnceSet swallows errors.

Close to the reference, but it adds a parenPos parameter to applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr that is meaningless when not wrapped (passed as 0), which is a slightly awkward API; it also lacks the Pretty fix.
Correct, with precise paren positions, but changes applyUnaryOpToDurationExpr's signature with a 0 sentinel for the non-wrapped case.
Minimal fix: wraps the literal in the paren rule and recurses in applyUnaryOp with a range check; it works, but the inner StartPos is set to the operator position and Pretty is not updated.
Minimal, correct wrap in paren_duration_expr plus a recursive call for the unary-paren path; adds a redundant range check and leaves Pretty unfixed.
Reference-like approach that includes the Pretty unary-plus fix and a parse-time check for (0); that check only covers the (N) form, and the test outputs are redundantly duplicated.

Wraps a bare NumberLiteral as a Wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr in both the paren and unary paths, fixes Pretty to match String, and keeps the parse-time error for `foo[(0)]` (but not for `foo[-(5)]`), with good round-trip and error tests.
Correct wrapping, with constant-value checks that preserve positive and divide-by-zero parse errors; it is reasonable but adds no tests for those preserved errors and no Pretty fix.
Correct wrap, and extends the positive and div/mod checks through unary/paren wrappers, but adds no tests for those new validations and sets StartPos inside the paren.

Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral and changes its String(), yet still has to convert to a DurationExpr via asDurationExpr; this dual mechanism works but is more invasive and convoluted than lifting the literal as the reference does.
Same NumberLiteral.Wrapped AST change as C4, plus a new rule action and broadened div/mod/positive checks; correct, but spreads changes across the AST, printer and grammar.

Nearly identical in structure to the reference (wrapDurationExpr applied in both the paren rule and applyUnaryOp), with good round-trip tests and a duration-visitor test; only the Pretty tweak is missing.
Closely mirrors the reference with a single wrapDurationExpr helper used by both the paren and unary paths, and adds a runtime evaluation test; it lacks only the Pretty fix.
Minimal and clean: wraps the literal in the paren rule and at the start of applyUnaryOp, and tests cover the issue's tables; only the Pretty update is absent.
Minimal and clean: one helper used in the paren and unary paths, with round-trip tests including the reference cases; no Pretty or validation follow-ups.
Focused fix with a helper and a range check on the wrapped literal; correct, but it has no Pretty fix and no error-case tests.
Minimal, correct fix with a redundant out-of-range check; tests cover the issue's round-trip cases.

Lifts parenthesised literals into a wrapped unary-plus DurationExpr, keeps the parse-time positive-duration check, and fixes Pretty like the reference; tests are strong (printer, parse, visitor), though paren_duration_expr does an unconditional *NumberLiteral assertion.
Thorough fix with prettier parity, a recursive positive-duration check, a precise paren position and a durations-visitor test, though `$2.(*NumberLiteral)` is an unconditional, fragile cast.

Round-trip works, but it also populates Range/Step/OriginalOffset alongside the *Expr fields, reorders the subquery step printing, and adds a new experimental-flag check, all of which are unnecessary AST/printer behavior changes.

Fixes round-trip but also sets both Range/RangeExpr and OriginalOffset/OriginalOffsetExpr at parse time, flips subquery step print priority, and adds an experimental-flag check, all beyond the issue's scope.
Small, correct fix in the paren rule and applyUnaryOp; the comment claiming the literal was already range-checked is dubious, and Pretty is not updated.
Small, correct fix wrapping literals in both paths, with adequate round-trip tests; no prettier or validation follow-ups.

Like C7, it adds a NumberLiteral.Wrapped field and a printer change and also converts to a DurationExpr for offset/range fields; this works but is a heavier, two-mechanism design that touches the public AST.

Adds a public Wrapped field to NumberLiteral, giving two representations of parenthesised durations and glue conversions in the offset and range paths; it works and naturally keeps the div-by-zero and positive checks, but is more invasive than needed.

Correct wrapping, plus constant-value helpers that keep parse-time positive and division-by-zero errors for (0); tests include error cases and promqltest evaluation, though the DurationExpr construction is duplicated inline.
Correct wrap that also preserves parse-time positive and division-by-zero errors, with parse-error and promqltest evaluation tests; DurationExpr construction is duplicated inline in two places.
Wraps literals in both grammar paths and keeps the positive-duration parse check, with good parse, printer and evaluation tests; the wrapping is inlined into grammar actions and Pretty is unchanged.
Correct wrap using paren positions plus a recursive positive-duration check, with error and eval tests; div/mod-by-(0) and Pretty are not addressed.
Works and preserves zero/div checks, but it uses an odd *Item pointer as the wrapped flag and includes a spurious generated-file header change from regenerating in the wrong directory.
Correct and covers positive and div/mod checks, but uses an awkward *Item parameter, adds a redundant range check, and changes the generated-file header through regeneration from another directory.
Clean helper used in both the paren rule and the unary-paren offset rule, and it preserves the positive-duration parse check; it skips the Pretty fix and adds no error-case tests.
Clean wrap helper used in both paths plus a recursive positive check, but the new validation is untested and Pretty is not updated.
Traps return in walkTemplate by unwrapping the ExecError and rewrites `return A | B` cleverly, but `try` swallows return and a bare return in a partial discards output and yields nil.

Relies on the ExecError-wrapped error path instead of a proper trap, so try swallows returns; bare return discards partial output; adds new AST-rewrite complexity (return A|B to A|B|return), against the issue's goal of removing transforms.

Avoids exec changes by letting the error travel as an ExecError and has correct HasValue semantics (package suite passes), but there is no walkTemplate trap, `try` swallows return, and it edits the forked parse/node.go.

Avoids executor changes by riding the ExecError path, so returns are not trapped at template/block boundaries (a return in baseof's main block kills the page) and try swallows them; also modifies the forked parse package.

Behaviour is thorough (trap in executeWithState and walkTemplate, try passthrough, HasValue) with an excellent unit test, but it changes the Executer interface and the executeWithState signature, which is more intrusive to the fork.

Traps return at executeWithState and walkTemplate, handles try, HasValue and the callable-args wrap, and has strong unit plus integration tests; extending the Executer interface is somewhat more intrusive to the fork.
Has no walkTemplate trap, so a bare return in a define exits everything; retained HasReturn makes a bare return yield nil, and arg wrapping only applies in partials, though the unit test is nice.
No walkTemplate trap, output discarded via HasReturn, args-wrapping only applied in partials, and no arg check.
Correct HasValue semantics, walkTemplate trap, arg grouping and good tests, but it does not stop `try` from swallowing return.
Good semantics (HasValue, template boundary, arg check) with thorough tests and docs, but it never re-panics in try, so try silently swallows a return.
The recoverReturn helper is tidy and handles walkTemplate, try and arg wrapping, but keeping HasReturn discards partial output, so a bare or unreached return gives nil, unlike the expected behaviour.

Carefully built (executeWithState and walkTemplate traps, try, HasReturn excludes subtemplates), but it deliberately discards partial output whenever a return exists, so a bare return yields nil, diverging from the reference.

Solid implementation covering the HasValue partial semantics, walkTemplate trap, try passthrough, arg normalization and arity check; it does not reject value returns outside partials or misplaced returns in pipelines.

Clean design: HasValue, try passthrough, walkTemplate trapping and arg-count check, with bare-return-returns-output semantics matching the reference; it does not enforce return-last-in-pipeline or error on valued returns outside partials.

Return does not stop at template boundaries, since walkTemplate never traps it, and a bare return in a partial yields nil instead of the rendered output; the `_returnNoop` function and the neutralizeReturn rewrite of decorator blocks are a hacky, questionable addition.
No walkTemplate trap, so a return inside a block or template call aborts the whole page; also adds an unrequested user-visible _returnNoop func and a neutralizeReturn AST pass.
Handles walkTemplate, try and HasValue correctly with good tests including try; it has no arity check, moves `return` to a new namespace, and contains a misleading docs sentence.
Correct core behaviour (template boundary, try, bare return keeps output) with good tests and docs; extra pipeline args to return are silently ignored.
Correct trapping incl. try passthrough and HasValue semantics with thorough tests; moving `return` to the templates namespace and changing ExecuteWithContextAndKey's signature are extra churn.

Solid implementation with HasValue semantics, try and template-boundary handling and an arg check; moves return to the templates namespace and changes the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature, which is acceptable but broader.
Without arg wrapping, the existing `return add . 42` form breaks, and a bare return in a partial yields nil.
Drops the args-wrapping transform, which breaks the documented {{ return add . 42 }} form; bare return discards partial output and there is no arg check.
Without arg wrapping, existing `{{ return add . 42 }}` usage regresses; it also keeps HasReturn so a bare or unreached return yields nil, and `try` swallows return.
Has no args-wrapping, breaking {{ return add . 42 }}; HasReturn makes partials with any return discard output; try is not handled.
Has no walkTemplate trap and a bare return yields nil; it also wraps whole pipelines into return and rewrites the existing 13600 regression test to the new semantics.
No template-boundary trap and bare return yields nil; rewrites the existing issue-13600 test into a different passing case to fit its pipeline-wrapping semantics.
Clean walkReturnable helper with correct HasValue semantics and broad tests, but `try` swallows return and changing the ExecuteWithContextAndKey signature is more invasive.
Clean walkReturnable helper and correct HasValue/output semantics, but no try passthrough, no arg-count check, and the docs contain undefined reference links.
Simple sentinel approach with arg wrapping and try handling, but a return in a `template`/`define` exits the whole template and a bare return in a partial yields nil.
Minimal approach with no walkTemplate trap, so a return in a block or template exits the entire template; bare return yields nil, and test coverage is thin.
Traps return in walkTemplate and passes it through try, but retains HasReturn/io.Discard so a bare return in a partial yields nil; arg wrapping only applies to callable first args.

Sound sentinel/panic design with try, template-boundary and arg-count handling, but it keeps HasReturn to discard output, so a bare or unreached return in a partial yields nil instead of the rendered output.
